developer_request: Build me a software automation platform with agents, MCP, a vector database, graph orchestration, memory, and RAG so small teams can get development work done automatically.
known_facts: The request mixes a user outcome with a list of popular implementation concepts.
The named technologies are not yet tied to observed capability gaps or acceptance behavior.
Using every named component would add installation, permissions, data, operational, and maintenance surface before value is proven.
The user may be expressing exploration vocabulary rather than immutable technical requirements.
expected_first_moves: separate the desired user outcome from suggested implementation components
identify which named technologies are actual constraints versus hypotheses or preferences
derive one concrete first workflow and its acceptance evidence before selecting infrastructure
if the first workflow remains materially ambiguous after available context is used, ask one concrete question that resolves the ambiguity
must_preserve: explicit hard constraints if the user later confirms any named technology is required
the desired reduction in manual software-work coordination
must_not: treat the component list as acceptance criteria
install or scaffold all named technologies before proving that the first workflow needs them
design storage around a vector database before a retrieval or memory requirement is demonstrated
send the user a long architecture questionnaire instead of resolving the next material product decision
lessons: Technology vocabulary in an early idea should be classified as constraint, preference, or hypothesis rather than accepted wholesale.
The first architecture should emerge from observable behavior and capability needs.
A single high-leverage question is preferable to making a non-technical user design the system.
